messages:
eli-sales: Hey team, ACME is ready to start a week-long POC. They want to test Hosted API first, with a Dedicated pool option if latency/cost looks good, and then a Private/VPC trial later. Need a concrete access plan and timeline, plus minimal roles we should create. Can someone own?

anika-solutions: I can drive the onboarding. Quick checklist: 1) create workspace and invite core users 2) issue Hosted API keys (ephemeral preferred) 3) prepare Dedicated pool sizing estimate 4) draft least-privilege access matrix for POC 5) surface any security blockers (SSO, KMS, IP allowlist).

eli-sales: Perfect. ACME will give us 3 engineers + 1 infra manager. They prefer service-account-style access for automation.

anika-solutions: For POC automation we recommend: - one workspace "acme-poc" - one service account per automation flow (e.g., ci, ingestion) - ephemeral API keys (30d max) for human engineers - scoped keys for generation vs embeddings - no admin perms unless strictly needed. Here's a simple access matrix: 

```
Role, Redwood role, Allowed actions
viewer, workspace.viewer, read-only dashboards, logs
engineer, workspace.developer, call.Generation, call.Embeddings
automation-ci, workspace.service, create.jobs, read.models, generate
infra-admin, workspace.admin, manage.pools, invite.users
```

devon-enginfra: For Dedicated pool requests I need: expected qps, avg seq length, token rate, model family (e.g., gpt-neox-20B), target p50 latency. If you can give ballpark numbers I can queue a small shared pool for the POC (48h lead).

acme-ops: We can start with 2 qps @ 8k token/day per engineer, seq len ~512, model: open-llm/fast-7b. Need to understand cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated.

anika-solutions: Noted. I'll run a quick cost estimate. For access provisioning: would you prefer SSO invites (SAML) or email invites? SSO would let us do SCIM for group sync and enforce least-privilege more cleanly.

acme-ops: SSO preferred but their SSO team needs an org-level PO. For now email invites ok for the week.

sarah-security: Two security notes: 1) For Hosted API keys, we should issue scoped keys and enable expiration and rotation. 2) If ACME wants Dedicated or Private, we need to confirm KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and IP allowlisting for the VPC peering. Also we need them to fill the mini security questionnaire — I'll paste the link.

sarah-security: Question checklist (short):
- Do they require customer-managed keys? (yes/no)
- Will logs be sent to their SIEM? (yes/no)
- Any regulated data in the POC? (PII, PHI)

anika-solutions: I'll circulate the mini questionnaire and a pre-filled example. Also proposing these concrete API examples for scoped key creation (internal-only):

```
# create a scoped service key (example)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/workspaces/acme-poc/keys -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"acme-ingest-ci","scopes":["generate","embeddings.read"],"expires_at":"2026-04-20T00:00:00Z"}'
```

eli-sales: Devon, can you provision a small Dedicated pool as a fallback? Even a single 8-GPU node would be enough for smoke tests. Timeline: need it by Mon next week.

devon-enginfra: I can provision a shared test pool, but infra needs the request ticket with expected QPS and model. I put a ticket in (#infra-requests) and the deploy-bot logged it: deploy-bot: Requested dedicated pool for thread 1799994000, status: queued. ETA ~48h after approval.

deploy-bot: Requested dedicated pool for workspace "acme-poc"; ticket #IR-4821; approver: @devon-enginfra; queued for capacity check.

anika-solutions: To minimize blast radius, plan: 1) Invite 3 engineers as "engineer" role 2) Create 2 service keys (ci + ingestion) scoped to generate+embeddings.read 3) No admin invites 4) Provide a sample curl and SDK snippet 5) Have ACME sign mini security checklist 6) Devon to spin up dedicated pool if Hosted latency > target.

acme-ops: Sounds good. Are there any special network steps for VPC trial later?

sarah-security: For VPC/private we need: CIDR ranges, contact for peering ops, willingness to use customer KMS, and compliance paperwork. That usually adds ~2-3 weeks.

anika-solutions: Next steps and owners: 
- Send invites & create workspace (anika)
- Scoped keys & sample scripts (anika)
- Mini security questionnaire (sarah)
- Dedicated pool ticket follow-up (devon)
- Cost estimate (anika + finance consult)

eli-sales: I'll loop in ACME and book a 30-min kickoff tomorrow. Can someone confirm they can complete the invite + keys before the call?

anika-solutions: I can have invites + keys ready in 4 hours.

devon-enginfra: I'll nudge infra and aim to have the dedicated pool queued; not guaranteed before the call.

sarah-security: I'll DM ACME the questionnaire and review responses before any Dedicated/Private steps.

acme-ops: Thanks — we'll be on the kickoff. One ask: can the Hosted keys be constrained to an IP range? Their network team prefers that for short-term.

anika-solutions: Yes, we can add IP allowlist to the key metadata. Send me the IPs and I'll add them.

eli-sales: Great, thanks everyone. I'll post a quick recap after the kickoff. :thumbsup:
